19.13.3.en: St. John Chrysostom They that dwell in mine house, and my maids, count me for a stranger.

19.14.0.en: I am an alien in their sight [15].

19.14.1.en: Even those whom he had brought into his house as sojourners and maids counted him a stranger to them. Not one of them stretched out a hand to serve him in the midst of his severe illness. If he called one of his servants and asked him for something, he left him without answering him a word, though he had been a merciful master to them and had not refused their right in their cause against him (Job 31:13).

19.14.2.en: * "They that dwell in mine house, and my maids, count me for a stranger" [15]. This is about the incarnate Lord, whom those who had long before announced Him in the words of the Law refused to know and honour...

19.14.3.en: "I am an alien in their sight" [15]. For our Redeemer, since the synagogue did not recognize Him, became like a stranger in His own house.

19.14.5.en: * "No prophet is accepted in his own country" (Lk 4:24). Since Anathoth was the homeland of Jeremiah (Jer 11:21), it did not receive him well. And Isaiah and the rest of the prophets were rejected by their homeland, that is, the people of the circumcision... But we, who did not belong to the covenant but were strangers from the promise, received Moses and the prophets who announce Christ, we received them with all our hearts more than the Jews, who rejected Christ and did not accept the testimony concerning Him.

19.14.6.en: Origen I called my servant, and he gave me no answer.

19.15.0.en: I intreated him with my mouth [16].

19.15.1.en: He is the master, entreating the servant and begging him, and the servant does not care and pays him no attention.

19.15.2.en: * "I called my servant, and he gave me no answer" [16]. It is clear that (Christ) was speaking about Judas.

19.16.0.en: * "I intreated him with my mouth; I besought my wife" [17]. (Christ) is speaking about Jerusalem, for He betrothed her to Himself so that she might serve the Law. He entreated many times for her sake in order to save her. He besought her many times to change, until He said: "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together... and ye would not!" (Mt 23:37).

19.16.1.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * Who are the Jewish people but a "servant" who did not obey the Lord out of love as a son?... God calls us when He brings us near by His gifts, and we answer the call when we serve Him worthily according to the benefits that we receive.

19.16.2.en: "I intreated him with my mouth" [16]. It is as though He says more clearly: I Myself, who accepted My incarnation, gave commandments to be practised, by the mouth of the prophets, and I came to him incarnate, entreating him with My mouth. Thus when Matthew (the Evangelist) told of the commandments that (the Lord) delivered on the mountain, he said: [And he opened his mouth, and taught them] (Mt 5:2). It is as though he says plainly: then He opened His mouth, He who had opened before the mouths of the prophets.

19.16.3.en: So too it was said of Him by the bride who longs for His tenderness: "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" (Song 1:2), through all the commandments that she learns by preaching. It is as though the holy Church receives the many kisses of His mouth. Now it was well said: "I intreated," since He appeared in the flesh, uttering the commandments of life in humility, as though seeking His servant who was full of pride, that perhaps he might come...

19.16.5.en: * O company of the Jews, when you come to Jerusalem and find that it has been laid waste and turned into dust and ashes, do not weep like children (1 Cor 14:20)(d). Do not grieve, but seek for yourselves a city in heaven instead of the one that you seek here on earth. Lift up your eyes, and you will find on high the Jerusalem which is free, which is the mother of us all (Gal 4:26).

19.16.6.en: Do not grieve over the absence of the temple here, and do not despair at your lack of a priest. For in heaven you will find an altar and the priests of the good things to come, after the order of Melchizedek, in their procession before God (Heb 5:10). For the love and mercy of the Lord willed to take from you the earthly inheritance, so that it might be possible for you to seek the heavenly.

19.16.7.en: Origen My breath is strange to my wife, and I am loathsome (and foul) to the children of my own body [17].

19.16.8.en: As for his wife, she could no longer bear to come near him or endure the smell of his sores. Although he treated her with conjugal love, she made light of him and despised him.

19.16.9.en: * "I besought the sons of my concubines" [17 LXX]. In the same way as we understand the servant to be the synagogue of the Jews, so also the concubines. As we spoke of the associates (Job 19:15) as being the scribes and Pharisees, on account of the Holy Scripture, so also here [the sons]. It is about this (the synagogue established for Christ) that the Jewish people cries out through the prophet Isaiah: "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" (Isa 1:2). Often I called them, lamenting, and rebuking in anger, and comforting, and correcting.

19.16.10.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * "My wife shudders at my breath" [17]. What is this wife of the Lord but the synagogue of the Jews, subject to Him by the covenant of the Law in a carnal understanding? Now breath comes from the body, and unbelieving people understand the incarnation of the Lord in a carnal way, counting Him a mere man.

19.16.11.en: * "I besought the sons of my womb" [17]. God, who cannot be limited in a bodily way, is spoken of in such a manner, using members to show forth His power... Here the womb (the bowels) that conceives brings forth this life. Now what are we to understand by the "womb" but His counsel?

19.16.13.en: * The prophet Zechariah took up the harp of the Spirit and ran before Him with prophetic hymns; with joy he tuned its strings and moved his voice, and said: "Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion"... Rejoice and cry out with the glory on high, for He comes to you as I told you by prophecy.

19.16.14.en: But the contemptible bride (the company of the Jews who refused to be His bride)... did not rejoice as she was called, but was crushed and grieved at the coming of the Bridegroom. And for this reason she did not rejoice in receiving Him.

19.16.15.en: Her heart was captured by the (golden) calf, her beloved, and with it she bargains, and she does not want to listen to the prophet who says to her: "Rejoice greatly."

19.16.16.en: She did not go out to carry branches with the children...!

19.16.17.en: The prophets knock at her high gates and awaken her, but she is asleep in her love for her many companions!

19.16.18.en: The children glorify the coming (heavenly) King and bless Him, while the old woman is busy cleaning her idols (their self-love and the pride of their hearts).

19.16.19.en: She grieved at the coming of the Father's heir. She knew that He would expose her, so she hated Him, and was not willing for the children to glorify Him!

19.16.20.en: Envy struck her mouth dumb, so she became mute, silent from glorifying, and was busy with silencing those who glorify!

19.16.21.en: It was not enough for her that she did not want to glorify; she also strove to silence those who glorify!

19.16.22.en: These glorified Him, but she was angry at their voices.

19.16.23.en: Isaiah cried out: Awake, awake, put on strength.

19.16.24.en: Zechariah cried out: Rejoice and be glad at the coming King.

19.16.25.en: The children cried out: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

19.16.26.en: She listened neither to the prophets nor to the children, but grieved at their voices and was angry.

19.16.27.en: O Jews, haters of the light, how can you keep silent about the glorification that fills heaven and earth?

19.16.28.en: St. Jacob of Serugh Yea, young children despised me.

19.17.0.en: I arose, and they spake against me [18].

19.17.1.en: Perhaps he means here the children of his servants, who were born in his house and whom he counted as his own children; they mocked him and spoke evil against him. When he had authority over them he showed them all love, and when he lost his authority they insulted him and mocked him.

19.17.2.en: * [When I departed from them, they spake against me] [18]. It is as though the Lord drew near to the hearts of men when He wrought wonders for them. And it is as though He departed from them when He did not show them signs. But they spoke against the Lord as against one who had departed when they refused to submit to Him by faith... Moreover he added that the teachers of the Law and the Pharisees [and those whom he loved much are turned against him]. For by their readiness for unbelief they turned away from faith in the truth... and even persecuted Him.

19.18.0.en: All my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me [19].

19.18.1.en: None of those around him offered him anything any longer but hatred; all the scales had been overturned.

19.19.s.en: 4. The loss of anyone to show him tenderness

19.19.0.en: 20 My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth. 21 Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; for the hand of God hath touched me. 22 Why do ye persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?

19.19.1.en: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth [20].

19.19.2.en: After complaining of what God had permitted for him, in that He hemmed in the way before him and besieged him so that he had no outlet, and kindled the fires of His wrath against him; stirred up strangers (raiders) against him and gave them power against him; and all his relatives, friends, household, servants and slaves took a stand of hatred - now he complains of his body, which had almost dissolved. His freshness, beauty and strength were gone from him, and no health was left in him, until his bone cleaved to his skin, and he became a skeleton. Even his skin had almost dissolved, so that nothing was left to him but the skin of his teeth.

19.19.3.en: * "My flesh is corrupted under my skin, and my bones are held by the teeth" [20]. It is understood from these words that he speaks of the mystery of the Lord, for the whole of humanity may fittingly be called "skin," especially the churches and their assemblies. In them and for them the body of the Lord did not see corruption, for His body would not see corruption (Ps 16:10). But in respect of the truth of His descent from the heavens for the sake of suffering, He shared in some way in the food of the pious. For Job is not speaking of a dissolution that belongs to corruption, but is speaking of the part of food (spiritual), for Christ became food that is offered and taken by our teeth. We could not have partaken of the Lord's body had He not willed to draw near to us and to let us taste His body.

19.20.0.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; for the hand of God hath touched me [21].

19.20.1.en: After giving the preceding painful description of his state, he asked his friends to have pity on him. He had fallen under the wrath of God, and this is the harshest of all calamities, so let them have pity on him and show him practical love by prayer and supplication to God for his sake, instead of their persecuting him.

19.20.2.en: * How noble Job was when he was in trial, for he said: "Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends" (Job 19:21). It is not a cry as from misery, but rather from one who reproaches. For when his friends rebuked him unjustly he answered them: [Have pity upon me, O my friends], that is, it was fitting for you to show tenderness, but you attacked and crushed a man on whom you should have had compassion in his sufferings for the sake of friendship.

19.20.3.en: St. Ambrose * Notice that he calls them "friends," those who insult him, for to pious minds what is against them is counted for their benefit. For any wicked man either is changed by the sweetness of the righteous, so that he turns back from his wickedness and thereby becomes a friend, or he holds fast to his wickedness and becomes a friend against his will...

19.20.4.en: Job was struck by Satan, and yet he did not ascribe the stroke to Satan but called it "the hand of God hath touched me," just as Satan himself said: "But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face" (Job 2:5). For the holy man knew that what Satan himself did from his own evil will, he received authority for not from himself, but from the Lord.

19.20.6.en: * Friendship cannot be strong unless you are united with your friend and cleave to him by that love which the Holy Spirit, given to us, pours out.

19.20.7.en: * We must conform to all in order to gain all, following the Apostle, who said of himself: "I am made all things to all men, that I might by all means save some" (1 Cor 9:22). Be sorrowful with the sorrowful, for there is nothing that comforts a sorrowful man like seeing someone grieve with him over his hardship, and joyful with the joyful, and weak with the weak. But this accompaniment is necessary to help one's neighbour and to save him from his evil, not to share in his evil.

19.20.8.en: See how a man bends down to raise up with his hand one who has fallen; he does not fall with him in order to raise him, but stands firm with his feet on the ground lest he fall because of the one who has fallen, then stretches his hand to him a little, as far as he needs help, and thereby lifts him from his fall.

19.20.9.en: Let this be a fitting picture for us: we must bend down a little, and accompany them a short way in their circumstances, in order to save them from their falls and to gain them for God. But for this we must keep our hearts firm lest they draw us after them.

19.21.0.en: St. Augustine Why do ye persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh? [22]

19.21.1.en: If God is pursuing him, it is for a reason that no one knows; is this not enough? Why do they also pursue him? God has absolute authority over him, and His wisdom surpasses all human thought, so why do they too bring distress upon him?

19.21.2.en: If they rejoiced in his calamities, let them be content with his flesh, which was about to dissolve completely; why do they wound his spirit and shatter his psyche?

19.21.3.en: * He did not say that God persecuted him in a way opposed to his godliness. For there is a good persecutor, as the Lord says of Himself by the lips of the prophet: [Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off] (Ps 101:5). And when the saint suffers the stroke he realizes that he suffers a persecution in return for the evil he committed inwardly...

19.21.4.en: It is as though he says: why do you persecute me for my weaknesses, as if you yourselves were without weakness in the likeness of God...?

19.21.5.en: He rightly added: [And are not satisfied with my flesh]. For the mind that hungers to punish its neighbour necessarily seeks to be satisfied with the flesh of another. Moreover it must be known that those who feed on slander of the life of others are surely those who [are satisfied with the flesh] of others. So Solomon says: "Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh" (Prov 23:20). For one who brings a body to eat it is, in the language of baseness, to tell what is bad in the features of the brethren, and his punishment is: "For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags" (Prov 23:21). Those who get drunk give themselves up to cups, but the gluttons are those who utter slanders, contributing with words, like one who contributes to providing supplies to be eaten... And as it is written: [Every talebearer shall be rooted out](e), but the sluggard (the sleeper) clothes a man with rags, and his death finds him an object of mockery, empty of all good works.

19.21.7.en: When Fr. Dorotheus spoke about [not judging our neighbour], he spoke at length about our obligation not to usurp God's right of judgment, for He alone knows every soul, its strength and its inclinations, a man's gifts, his biological make-up and his abilities, and the circumstances that surround him. On the basis of all this it is He who condemns or justifies. We may indeed know a man who has committed a certain sin, perhaps one so clear that it needs no investigation, but can we judge the man as a whole because of a sin or sins that he committed at some time, when we do not know his depths or his circumstances?!

19.21.8.en: * God alone judges; it is for Him to justify and for Him to condemn. He knows the state of each one of us, our potentials and our deviations, our gifts, our circumstances and our dispositions, so He alone is to judge according to His unique knowledge. He judges the works of a bishop in one way, and the works of a superior in another; He judges an abbot of a monastery or his disciple differently; the old person (who has his experience and knowledge) differently from the one who seeks monasticism, and the sick differently from the one of sound health. Who can understand all these judgments except the Creator of all things, who knows all matters?

19.21.9.en: Fr. Dorotheus * See, my brethren, that the work of the servants at the wedding of the king's son (Mt 22) was nothing but to draw the good and the bad to the feast, and the Lord did not say of them that they judged those invited and distinguished between the good and the bad, nor did He say of them that they found one who had not on a wedding garment, but the king himself saw him; the master of the house alone discovered him and cast him out.

19.21.10.en: St. Augustine * Judging others is regarded as impudently robbing the divine right, while rebuking (without love) demolishes a man's soul.

19.22.0.en: 23 Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book! 24 That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever! 25 For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: 26 And though after my skin is destroyed, yet without my flesh shall I see God: 27 Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; my reins yearn within me.

19.22.1.en: Oh that my words were now written!

19.22.2.en: Oh that they were printed in a book [23]!

19.22.3.en: The following expressions reveal the splendour of Job's life, his hope, his thoughts and his concepts, and they lead us to reconsider the interpretation of all that has gone before, for even his speeches that seemed to carry sharp reproach, and which many commentators criticized as having overstepped his bounds, came from a heart that longs to see God.

19.22.4.en: In all the words of dialogue in this Book between Job and his friends we find nothing more eloquent than what is before us now. He speaks to us wonderfully of the Lord Christ and of heaven as a better homeland. He speaks of his faith in God the living Redeemer, and of the resurrection of the dead and the life of the age to come.

19.22.5.en: In the preceding expressions we smell the scent of despair and cut-off hope, but here the Spirit of God lifts him up, enlightens his insight, and grants him life-giving words.

19.22.6.en: Some hold that from these moments we no longer hear murmuring or complaint against God or His divine providence as before. For this reason they hold that the Holy Spirit of God, who knew the sincerity of his heart, the truth of his intention and his faith, lifted him up and tore the veil before him so that he might know the mystery of salvation and God's surpassing love; so the tone of his speech changed completely, and his soul found rest in Him in the midst of his sufferings.

19.22.7.en: Before, he was faithful and truthful, but he fixed his eyes, his heart and his mind on his friends, so he fell into a kind of frustration and was occupied with defending himself against the accusations directed at him by his friends. But now the Spirit lifted him up as to heaven and brought him in as to the throne of grace, and he saw the Messiah the Saviour coming, and his soul found rest in Him.

19.22.8.en: He began with a delightful introduction that reveals his surpassing heavenly peace, which he longs for every believer to enjoy. Therefore he says: "Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book!" It is as though he says: would that all would forget all that I said before; words came from me that were the fruit of my human wisdom and my human weakness, but now the Spirit of God leads me. Would that all might hear His voice with me and share with me in what I enjoy. I try to write it in letters, but words fail to express it. I will draw it in a book, perhaps the language of drawing will be more able than the language of letters!

19.22.9.en: * What prophecy is clearer than this? No one since the days of Christ has spoken plainly of the resurrection as he did (Job) before Christ. He longed that his words should remain for ever, that time should not blot them out, engraving them on a plate of lead and carving them on the rock (Job 19:23). He hopes for the resurrection. No, rather he saw Christ his Redeemer living, rising from the earth. The Lord had not yet died, and he saw the struggles of the Church, his Redeemer risen from the tomb. When he says: [And I shall put on again my skin, and see God in my flesh](f), I do not think he speaks as one who loves his body, since it had decayed and dissolved before his eyes, but in the certainty of his rising again, and through the consolations of the future he lit up his wretched present.

19.23.0.en: St. Jerome That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever [24].

19.23.1.en: He wishes to direct the words to all the coming generations, and that they should remain a constitution for mankind for ever. He longs that they be engraved on stone with an iron pen and then lead be poured into the engraving, so that time may not wear them away and they may not escape the eyes of any man. Let them be an inscribed monument bearing witness to God's work in the believer throughout the generations.

19.23.2.en: Records were kept in three ways: 1. By writing them in a book of cloth or skin or leaves of trees such as papyrus. From the latter word came the English word paper. Sometimes the inner bark of trees was used for writing. The Latin expression Liber was used for a book, and from it came the word "Library." 2. Lead tablets, which are very ancient. In 1699 Montfaucon bought in Rome a very ancient book made of lead: a collection of lead tablets fastened with lead nails and hinges. The book contains Egyptian Gnostic figures with Greek and Etruscan inscriptions.

19.23.3.en: In a temple in the city of Cnidus a monument of hell was found dating from the fourth century B.C., on which women appear depositing thin sheets of lead on which were written the names of the persons they hated together with their evil deeds. Curses that would fall on those who had wronged them were also engraved on the lead tablets. Many of these tablets were discovered in 1858 A.D. during the excavations in the ruins of the temple, and they are now deposited in the British Museum.

19.23.4.en: Righteous Job refers here to lead tablets or (tree) leaves with inscriptions on them. Perhaps he alludes here to the custom of engraving letters on stone and pouring molten lead into the engraving. 3. Stone monuments: the Law was engraved on two tablets of stone by the finger of God (Ex 31:18). Another set of two stones was written by Moses by divine command (Ex 34:4, 8). Also Joshua wrote a copy of the Law of Moses before the children of Israel on stones (Josh 8:32).

19.23.5.en: Job wanted his feelings to be engraved on stones so that coming generations might benefit from them.

19.24.0.en: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth [25].

19.24.1.en: [I know that my redeemer liveth.] He believed in the coming Redeemer, and that He is his life. "And that he shall stand upon the earth (at the latter day)." He awaits the coming of the Messiah, the incarnate Word of God, who comes in the fullness of time incarnate to walk among us on our earth.

19.24.2.en: Some hold that he speaks here of His last coming, when He comes on the clouds, and meets us human beings as earthly creatures, and brings us into the fellowship of His glories.

19.24.3.en: The word [redeemer], as it appears in the Law (Lev 25:25), is the one who has the right to redeem what his brother has sold or pledged. Our heavenly inheritance was sold because of sin, and One came to restore it to us, redeeming it with His blood as the price. Our Christ is the living Redeemer, who alone is able to pay our debt, remove the pledge and restore to us the eternal inheritance.

19.24.4.en: He will come on the clouds, but as upon the earth, where He commands the dead, and they rise from their graves, and He brings them into immortality and incorruption.

19.24.5.en: * "For I know that he is eternal who saves me on the earth, he will raise up my skin which endures all these things" [25]. This is the reason Job said: [My words are written for the coming generations], for after the sufferings they will learn the resurrection... It is clear that the body that receives sufferings rises.

19.24.6.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * [I know that he is eternal, who saves me on the earth] [25]. This means that He who leads me on the earth is God. And what does this mean? If God is immortal, why do you want these words to be written, and their memory to remain for ever in an immortal way? Notice the state of the souls of those who are in distress. They seek not only eyewitnesses of it, but that those who come later should also become witnesses of their misfortunes, in a way by which they obtain sympathy from every side. It is like the case of the rich man mentioned in the Gospel (Lk 16:19), who thought that he wanted those on earth to know his distress and the state he had come to. These were those who in those days were in prosperity.

19.24.7.en: * [And I shall rise in the last day from the earth] [25]. This is because the resurrection that he announced in his own person He will one day bring about in us also... He gave us its pledge so that the members may follow the glory of their head (Christ). Our Redeemer passed through death, so we do not fear death. He showed the resurrection, so that we might have a firm hope that we too are able to rise.

19.24.8.en: St. John Chrysostom * This man in truth abstained from every evil work, for he did not allow the sin in him to master him, and when an unseemly thought rose in him he did not allow it to ascend to the head, and consequently did not allow it to be practised in act. For the presence of sin is one thing, and refusing to obey its desires is another.

19.25.0.en: St. Augustine And though after my skin is destroyed, yet without my flesh shall I see God [26].

19.25.1.en: Job was sure of the perishing of his body in the grave, and he spoke of it without concern: [and after my skin is destroyed here]. Without this body he sees God. It is as though he says to them: you have fixed your eyes on my body with all its afflictions, but I know that it will surely become food for worms, and even my skin will end like my flesh, but what delights my soul is that I see God.

19.25.2.en: St. Augustine holds that the word "skin" refers to our acceptance of death. The destruction of our skin points to our being rid of the state of inner mortification and inner corruption, that we may receive the resurrection of the soul and its incorruption. By this we enjoy the sight of the eternal, all-holy God. In other words, by the Holy Spirit of God we put off the works of our outer man until it perishes, and put on the works of the new man, who is after the image of his Creator, so that our Christ is revealed before our inner sight.

19.26.0.en: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; my reins yearn within me [27].

19.26.1.en: In the spirit of prophecy he beheld the coming of the Lord Christ, the incarnate Word of God, when He can be seen with the eyes of the body. He Himself, in His divinity, is not seen by the body, but the depths of the soul long for Him.

19.26.2.en: "Whom I shall see for myself," that is, I shall see Him and rejoice in Him, for He is the secret of my soul's happiness.

19.26.3.en: I shall see Him as He is (1 Jn 3:2) and not another. On the last day we shall see the Messiah, the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever. He is the One for whom my soul groans within me in longing.

19.26.4.en: * Every mind is lifted up and shaped in prayer according to its purity. If it is concerned with material, earthly things, it carries this outlook before it, and this outlook remains before the inner eyes of its soul in its vision of the Lord Jesus, whether when He came in His humility in the flesh, or at His coming in His majesty. Such as these cannot see the Lord Jesus coming in His kingdom, for they are held by a kind of Jewish weakness (that is, the material outlook), and cannot say with the Apostle: "Yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we him no more" (2 Cor 16:5).

19.26.5.en: But those who rise above earthly, lowly works and thoughts, and ascend the high mountain of solitude (seclusion), freed from the disturbance of all earthly troubles and thoughts, safe from the intrusion of sins, glorifying with strong faith, these can look with pure eyes upon His divinity, and in the heights of virtue they discover His glory and the image of His exaltation...

19.26.6.en: Jesus reveals Himself to those who are in the cities and villages and farms, that is, those who have work to do, but not with the splendour with which He appears to those who ascend with Him the aforementioned mountain of virtues... For in solitude (seclusion) God appeared to Moses and spoke with Elijah.

19.26.7.en: Fr. Isaac * Be careful of the purity of your body and the soundness of your heart, for if you make sure of obtaining them you will see God your Lord.

19.27.0.en: But ye should say, Why persecute we him?

19.27.1.en: Seeing the root of the matter is found in me [28].

19.27.2.en: Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath bringeth the punishments of the sword.

19.28.0.en: That ye may know there is a judgment [29].

19.28.1.en: Job tells them what they ought to say: "Why persecute we him?" Why do we grieve him and provoke him by our criticism of his dealings, for the root of the matter is in me.

19.28.2.en: As he reveals his joy at seeing his Redeemer, whom his soul desires, he warns them to fear the day of His coming lest they be judged because of their judging of their brethren (Mt 7:1; Jas 2:1).

19.28.3.en: * [For ye say: What shall we say before him, and thus we find the root of the word in him] (Job 19:28) LXX. It is clear that under the influence of the work of the spirit of prophecy Job says this about the Pharisees and scribes and others in authority among the Jewish people. For they look to find something to say against Him (Mt 26:59)(g). That is, they wanted to find a pretext to criticize and blame Him, whether for His words or for His conduct. But what does He say to them? Do you beware of deceit? For since I uncover what is hidden and proclaim the mysteries, you deserve many chastisements not only because of your words but also because of your thoughts, so that you may not be asked about this afterward.

19.28.4.en: "For wrath will come upon the wicked, and then they will know where their being is" (Job 19:29). Who is wicked like the Jewish people, who crucified the Giver of the Law with lawbreakers, and killed Him among robbers (Mt 27:38), He who preached contempt for riches? But wrath came upon them, when the city was burned with fire, and the temple was destroyed, and their pride was extinguished...

19.28.6.en: Who can support me but You!

19.28.7.en: * I believe that You are the Ruler of all; nothing will happen without Your will, or without Your permission.

19.28.8.en: * In the midst of my distress, I see even the members of my household turning into enemies.

19.28.9.en: I cry out to You from my depths:

19.28.10.en: Have You become an enemy to me, that You give me over to such distress?

19.28.11.en: How hard it is to see those who are mine become against me!

19.28.12.en: * In the midst of my trial, I was looking for tenderness from my loved ones!

19.28.13.en: The doors of their hearts were shut, that I might find the doors of Your heavens open before me.

19.28.14.en: In the midst of the bitterness of the trial I find sweetness in enjoying Your care.

19.28.15.en: * If the tongues of friends have become exceedingly biting, the tongues of Your own have turned into a deadly sword.

19.28.16.en: They aimed their accusations like spears against You!

19.28.17.en: If they stand against me, I remember how Your own stood against You, O Saviour of the whole world!

19.28.18.en: If they exalt themselves over me, who am dust and ashes, dust exalted itself over You, O Creator of heaven and earth!

19.28.19.en: If nets are wound about me, and snares are set in my path, the leaders conspired with the people against You!

19.28.20.en: * I often suffer from the feeling of isolation, but I see You, one with Your Father, crying out in my name:

19.28.21.en: My God, my God: why hast thou forsaken me?

19.28.22.en: Instead of the glory that by Your will You gave up for my sake, they put on You a crown of shame, and held You in contempt.

19.28.23.en: If they desire to kill me, I see You hanging on the Cross, and buried in the tomb, bearing me in Yourself, O Firstborn of the dead, so that I may pass through You into Your Father's bosom.

19.28.24.en: * At last I praise You and glorify You, You who have turned my bitter trial into the sweetness of contemplating You!

19.28.25.en: With every tribulation You carry me on the wings of the Spirit, that I may see You, and my soul rejoices!

19.28.26.en: Glory to You, who turn the crucible of trials into a new Mount Tabor.

19.28.27.en: I see You transfigured, occupied with nothing but speaking of the Cross, that I may ascend by it to You!
